How to play “Audit Mission Control — Day 8”

A guide for students. You can read it in five minutes. Every step is shown by a short animation recorded in the real game, so you can start to play by yourself.

420-D04-AB Conformity AssessmentDay 8 · Saturday, November 14, 2026Software configuration audits, part 2AEC Cybersecurity (LEA.D8) · CYB-01 · Fall 2026Student guide
The animations play one after the other, without a click. Good for a first look, alone or on the projector.

The game in four steps

The game is one HTML (HyperText Markup Language) file. It holds the lecture of Day 8 — Software configuration audits, part 2 — as eight missions. In every mission you first solve a problem from the audit of Érable Cycles (a fictional company). Then you read the slides that explain it. The game is formative: it is practice only and it does not count toward your grade.

1📂Open the game

Double-click the game file. It opens in your web browser.

2🗺️Choose the mission

On the map, click the mission that has a moving ring.

3▶Do the stages in order

In each stage: read, click your answer, then click Next stage ▶.

4⭐Finish the mission

At the last stage, click Finish the mission ✓. You win stars and a badge, and the next mission opens.

That is all you need to start. The rest of this page shows every step with an animation.

What you need
  • The game file: 420-D04-AB_Day08_Mission-Game_CYB-01_Fall-2026.html. Your professor gives it to you together with this guide.
  • A computer with a web browser: Chrome, Edge or Firefox.
  • Time: plan about 10 minutes for each mission. There are eight missions.
  • No Internet connection to play. Internet is needed only for the videos and the links.
How to read the animations
  • An amber frame shows where to look.
  • The black arrow is the mouse pointer.
  • A circle around the arrow means: the player clicks here.
  • 3what happensThe dark bar under the picture says what happens. Its number is the number of the step in the list next to the animation.
  • The amber line above the dark bar shows how far the animation is. At the end, the animation starts again.

Each animation is a GIF (Graphics Interchange Format) file. Under each animation: ↺ Replay starts it again from step 1, ⤢ Enlarge shows it larger, ⬇ Download saves it.

1Open the game

Good to know
  • There is nothing to install. There is no account and no password.
  • The game works without Internet. Only the videos and the links need Internet.
  • The game sends nothing to the Internet. Your points stay in your web browser, on your computer.
  • Use a computer if you can. On a phone the missions appear in two columns instead of a path; the game works the same way.
  1. 1
    Save the game file 420-D04-AB_Day08_Mission-Game_CYB-01_Fall-2026.html in a folder that you can find again, for example Documents.
  2. 2
    Double-click the file. It opens in your web browser. The page is named “420-D04-AB · Day 8 · Audit Mission Control (game)”.
  3. 3
    If the file opens in another program: right-click the file, choose Open with, then choose your browser (Chrome, Edge or Firefox).

2The screen of the game

  1. 1
    Your results are at the top right: your level, a bar that fills when you win points, your points in XP (experience points), and the number of badges you have won. Lv 1 · Intern means level 1, named Intern.
  2. 2
    Three pages. Missions is the page where you play. Library holds the slides, the cards, the questions, the videos and the links of the day. Progress shows your results.
  3. 3
    The stages. The green box lists the stages of every mission: Problem, Take it apart, Principle, Cards, Check.
  4. 4
    The mission map. Scroll down a little. The eight missions are on one path: the Warm-up on the left, Mission 7 on the right.
  5. 5
    The mission to play now has a moving ring: an amber ring that grows and fades around its circle.
  6. 6
    A mission with a lock is closed. If you click it, the game answers “Finish the previous mission first”.
One more button
  • Under the map there is a button Open every mission (teacher mode). It opens all the missions at once. Use it only if your professor asks you to: the missions are made to be played in order. A second click (Missions in order) closes them again.

3A mission has five stages

The stages are always in the same order. The next sections show them one by one.

1Problem→2Take it apart→3Principle→4Cards→5Check→✓Finish: stars + badge
StageWhat you doWhat you win
1. ProblemYou read a real situation and you make a first guess.+10 XP (experience points) if your first answer is right
2. Take it apartYou judge real evidence yourself, one item at a time.+5 XP for each item that is right on the first try
3. PrincipleYou read the slides that explain what you just did.+1 XP for each new slide
4. CardsYou answer five question cards out loud, you turn them and you rate yourself.+2 XP for each card marked ✓ I knew it
5. CheckYou answer six questions.+10 XP for each right answer
FinishYou click Finish the mission ✓.+20 XP, the badge of the mission and 1 to 3 stars
Two shorter missions
  • The Warm-up and Mission 7 have three stages only: Problem, Take it apart, Principle. They have no Cards and no Check.
  • You can open a stage again at any time: click its name in the list of stages under the title of the mission.

3.1Stage 1 — Problem

  1. 1
    On the map, click the mission that has the moving ring. The first time, it is the Warm-up.
  2. 2
    The mission opens. Under its title you see the list of its stages. The stage you are in is filled with green: 1. Problem.
  3. 3
    Read the situation in the yellow box, then the question under it.
  4. 4
    Click the answer that you think is right. A right answer turns green. If it is your first try, you win +10 XP (experience points).
  5. 5
    Click Next stage ▶ at the bottom right.
If your answer is wrong
  • Nothing is lost. The answer turns red and the game says why it is wrong. Then you choose again.
  • Only a right answer on the first try gives the 10 XP. Read the situation before you click.

3.2Stage 2 — Take it apart

  1. 1
    Read the evidence in the box: the rule (what is expected) and the value that was observed.
  2. 2
    Click the decision that you think is right. A wrong decision turns red. Nothing is lost.
  3. 3
    Choose again. The right decision turns green and the reason appears under the buttons.
  4. 4
    Click Next item ▶.
  5. 5
    Decide the next item. Right on the first try gives +5 XP (experience points). The coloured dots above the box count your results.
  6. 6
    Continue until the last item. Then the game shows your result for the stage, for example “2 of 3 right on the first try”.
  7. 7
    Click Next stage ▶.
The coloured dots
  • amber ring: the item you are on
  • green: right on the first try
  • red: right after one or more wrong tries
  • grey: not done yet

3.3Stage 3 — Principle

  1. 1
    Stage 3 shows the slides of the lesson. They explain what you just did in stages 1 and 2.
  2. 2
    Read the key message (yellow) and the explanation on the right of the slide.
  3. 3
    Click ▶ under the slide to read the next slide. ◀ goes back. Each new slide gives +1 XP (experience points).
  4. 4
    Enlarge opens the slide in a large viewer. In the viewer, the ← and → keys of the keyboard change the slide.
  5. 5
    Close ✕ closes the viewer and returns to the mission. Esc (Escape key) does the same.
After the slides
  • When you have read the slides, click Next stage ▶.
  • In the Warm-up and in Mission 7, stage 3 is the last stage: the button is Finish the mission ✓.
  • Missions 1 to 6 give two short videos under the slides. ▶ Watch on YouTube opens a video in a new tab (Internet needed). check on VirusTotal opens the VirusTotal site with the address of the video, so that you can check the link before you open it.

3.4Stage 4 — Cards

The animation starts at the end of stage 3 of Mission 1, where the two videos are. Then it shows the cards.

  1. 1
    Stage 4 shows five cards. Each card has a question. Read one question and say your answer out loud.
  2. 2
    Click the card. It turns and shows the answer. Compare it with your answer.
  3. 3
    Click ✓ I knew it if your answer was right: you win +2 XP (experience points). Be honest: the cards are for you.
  4. 4
    Click ↻ Not yet if you did not know the answer. It gives no points. Read this card again later.
  5. 5
    After the five cards, click Next stage ▶.
Why say the answer out loud
  • If you say (or write) your answer before you turn the card, you see at once whether you really knew it.

3.5Stage 5 — Check

  1. 1
    Stage 5 has six questions. The label above each question gives its type. An MCQ (multiple-choice question) has one right answer.
  2. 2
    If you are not sure, click Hint. A short hint appears under the buttons.
  3. 3
    Click the answer you choose. It gets a coloured frame. You can still click another answer to change your choice.
  4. 4
    Click Check my answer. The right answer turns green. An answer you chose that is wrong turns red. Every option shows why it is right or wrong. A right answer gives +10 XP (experience points).
  5. 5
    Click Next question ▶.
  6. 6
    An MSQ (multiple-select question) has several right answers. The number in round brackets says how many, for example (3).
  7. 7
    Click all the right answers, then click Check my answer. The answer is correct only with all the right options and no wrong option.
After question 6
  • The button becomes Finish the mission ▶. Click it to finish the mission.
  • If you click Check my answer without an answer, the game says “Select an answer first”.
Label in the gameMeaningWhat you do
MCQ — one answer (1)One option is right.Click one option. A second click on another option replaces your choice.
MSQ — select all that apply (3)Several options are right. The number in round brackets is the number of right options.Click every right option. Click an option again to remove it.

4Finish a mission: stars, badge, next mission

  1. 1
    At the last stage, click Finish the mission ✓. In Missions 1 to 6, it is the button Finish the mission ▶ after question 6.
  2. 2
    The game shows Mission complete. You win +20 XP (experience points) and the badge of the mission.
  3. 3
    You also win 1, 2 or 3 stars. In the animation the player has 1 star, because one decision of stage 2 was wrong on the first try.
  4. 4
    ↻ Play it again starts the same mission again. Use it to win more stars. The game keeps your best number of stars.
  5. 5
    Next mission ▶ opens the next mission directly.
  6. 6
    Mission map returns to the map.
  7. 7
    On the map, your stars are under the mission. The next mission is now open: it has the moving ring.

How the stars are counted

Mission★★★ 3 stars★★☆ 2 stars★☆☆ 1 star
Missions 1 to 6 — the six questions of stage 5 (Check)5 or 6 right answers4 right answers3 right answers or fewer
Warm-up — the 3 items of stage 2, right on the first try3 of 3—2 of 3 or fewer
Mission 7 — the 6 steps and the 3 items of stage 2, right on the first try9 of 97 or 8 of 96 of 9 or fewer

5The last mission: put the steps in order

  1. 1
    Mission 7 is the last mission. Its stage 2 has one activity that the other missions do not have: you see the six steps of Lab 3 Part B in a mixed order.
  2. 2
    Click the step that you think comes first. If it is not the right one, it shakes and the game shows a short message. Nothing is lost.
  3. 3
    Choose another step. A right step moves to the top of the list, turns green and shows its code (B1, B2, …) and its details. It gives +5 XP (experience points) when you find it without a wrong click.
  4. 4
    Continue with the step that comes next, until the six steps are in order. Then answer three short questions, as in the other missions.

8Your progress

  1. 1
    Click Progress at the top of the page.
  2. 2
    The first line shows your XP (experience points), your level, the missions you have finished, your stars and the number of slides you have read.
  3. 3
    Under it are the eleven badges. A badge in colour is won. A grey badge is still to win.
  4. 4
    Erase my progress sets everything back to zero. The game asks you to confirm before it erases.
Where your progress is kept
  • The game saves your progress by itself, in your web browser, on your computer. There is no Save button.
  • You can close the page at any time. Open the same file again in the same browser: your XP, your stars and your badges are there.
  • Your progress does not follow you to another browser or to another computer.
  • A private window (incognito) does not keep your progress.
  • Do not move or rename the game file after you start: some browsers then count it as a new game.

9Help: problems and solutions

The mission has a lock.

Finish the mission before it: go to its last stage and click Finish the mission ✓.

I clicked a wrong answer.

Nothing is lost. The answer turns red and you choose again. Later, ↻ Play it again lets you win the points you missed.

I closed the browser by mistake.

Open the game file again in the same browser. Your progress is still there. Click your mission on the map to continue.

My points are gone.

The progress is kept by one browser on one computer. Check that you use the same browser, a normal window (not a private one) and the same file in the same folder.

A video or a link does not open.

Videos and links need Internet. Everything else in the game works without Internet.

The slide is too small to read.

Click Enlarge. You can also make the whole page larger: hold Ctrl (Control key) and press + (Ctrl and − makes the page smaller).

I want to read a stage again.

Click the name of the stage in the list under the title of the mission, for example 3. Principle.

I want to start again from zero.

Open Progress, click Erase my progress and confirm.

Does the game count toward my grade?

No. The game is formative: it is practice only.
